title: NHS Trust Admits to Unnecessary Breast Surgeries
subtitle: New findings reveal that dozens of patients suffered harm due to medical errors at a hospital trust in north-east England.

summary.en: A hospital trust in north-east England has admitted that twenty women had their breasts removed unnecessarily. The County Durham and Darlington foundation trust is currently reviewing hundreds of cases of past care. Many patients suffered harm because their cancer was missed or treated incorrectly. The trust has apologized for the failures and is working to support those affected. Police are also investigating whether any criminal actions occurred during these treatments.
summary.zh: 英格蘭東北部的一家醫院信託機構坦承，有二十名女性接受了不必要的乳房切除手術。達勒姆郡與達靈頓基金會信託目前正審查數百起過往的醫療病例。許多病患因癌症漏診或治療不當而受害。該機構已為這些疏失道歉，並致力於協助受影響的民眾。警方也正在調查這些治療過程中是否涉及任何刑事犯罪行為。

paragraphs.en: A major healthcare provider in north-east England has confirmed that twenty women underwent unnecessary breast removal surgeries due to serious mistakes in their medical care. The County Durham and Darlington foundation trust (CDDFT) recently admitted that these women were part of a much larger group of patients who experienced harm while receiving treatment at its breast unit. This news follows earlier reports that more than 200 patients had suffered because of poor care at the same hospital group.
paragraphs.zh: 位於英格蘭東北部的一家大型醫療保健機構證實，有二十名女性因醫療照護上的嚴重疏失，接受了不必要的乳房切除手術。達勒姆郡與達靈頓基金會信託（County Durham and Darlington foundation trust，簡稱 CDDFT）近期坦承，這些女性僅是該機構乳房診療單位在提供治療過程中，遭受損害的眾多病患之一。在此之前，已有報導指出該醫院體系內有超過兩百名病患因照護品質低落而受害。

paragraphs.en: Steve Russell, the chief executive of the CDDFT, expressed deep regret regarding the situation. He stated that the trust is very sorry to the women and their families who were let down by failures in the hospital's breast services. According to The Guardian Health, the trust recognizes that it should have listened more carefully to concerns and acted much sooner to prevent these problems. The hospital has since made significant changes to its breast service to improve safety for current and future patients.
paragraphs.zh: CDDFT 執行長羅素（Steve Russell）對此情況表達了深切的遺憾。他表示，信託機構對於醫院乳房診療服務的缺失，導致病患及其家屬受到傷害，深感抱歉。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，該機構承認當時應更審慎傾聽各界疑慮，並採取更迅速的行動以防止這些問題發生。該醫院隨後已對其乳房診療服務進行重大改革，以提升現有及未來病患的醫療安全。

paragraphs.en: As part of an ongoing effort to address these errors, the trust is conducting a detailed review of breast cancer cases from January 2023 to February 2025. They are also examining the experiences of 640 former patients who reached out through a special support line. The Guardian Health reports that out of 514 cases reviewed so far, 315 patients were found to have suffered harm. Of those, 77 patients experienced significant harm, and the trust confirmed that one patient has died. In some of these cases, doctors failed to identify cancer early, which allowed the disease to spread to other parts of the body.
paragraphs.zh: 作為解決這些錯誤的持續努力之一，該信託機構正針對二零二三年一月至二零二五年二月期間的乳癌病例進行詳細審查。他們同時也在檢視透過專屬支援專線聯繫的六百四十名前病患的就醫經驗。《衛報健康》報導指出，在目前已審查的五百一十四個病例中，有三百一十五名病患被認定受到損害。其中，七十七名病患遭受嚴重損害，且該機構證實有一名病患不幸死亡。在部分案例中，醫師未能及早診斷出癌症，導致病情擴散至身體其他部位。

paragraphs.en: For many patients, the impact of these mistakes has been life-changing. One woman, known as Jo, shared her story about receiving an unnecessary mastectomy—a surgery to remove all or part of a breast. She explained that further tests would have shown the other areas were healthy and that the cancer was very small. She described the experience as devastating, noting that losing a part of her body that is central to her identity was incredibly difficult to accept. Another patient, Denise Howarth, was told after her surgery and follow-up treatments that the operation on her breast had not been necessary at all.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多病患而言，這些錯誤造成的影響足以改變一生。一名化名為喬（Jo）的女性分享了她接受不必要乳房切除手術的經歷，這項手術旨在移除部分或全部乳房組織。她解釋說，若當時進行進一步檢查，便能顯示其他部位是健康的，且當時的癌細胞非常微小。她形容這段經歷令人崩潰，並指出失去身體的一部分對她的自我認同至關重要，這讓她極難接受。另一名病患豪沃斯（Denise Howarth）則是在手術及後續治療結束後，才被告知當初的乳房手術根本沒有必要。

paragraphs.en: This situation is now the subject of a wider investigation. The National Crime Agency is working alongside local police to look into claims made by former patients. The goal is to determine if any criminal offences took place during the time these patients were under the care of the hospital. This investigation is part of a broader period of scrutiny for the National Health Service (NHS), which has recently faced intense pressure following other reports of hospital management failures and poor patient safety across the country.
paragraphs.zh: 此事件目前正接受更廣泛的調查。英國國家犯罪局（National Crime Agency）正與當地警方合作，深入調查前病患提出的指控。調查目標在於釐清這些病患在該醫院接受照護期間，是否發生任何刑事犯罪行為。此次調查是英國國家醫療保健服務（NHS）面臨全面檢視的一環，該體系近期因國內其他醫院管理失當及病患安全問題頻傳，而承受巨大壓力。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the trust is preparing to discuss the next steps of its review process. On September 24, the trust board will meet in public to decide on the future scope and timeframe for checking past care. The hospital has promised to remain open about its findings and will provide further updates after the board meeting. In the meantime, the trust continues to offer a dedicated support line for anyone who is worried about the breast care they received. As the investigation continues, the focus remains on identifying all patients who were harmed and ensuring they receive the information and support they need to move forward.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，該信託機構正準備討論審查程序的後續步驟。九月二十四日，信託董事會將召開公開會議，決定未來審查過往醫療照護的範圍與時程。醫院承諾將保持公開透明，並會在董事會會議後提供進一步更新。在此期間，該機構持續為任何擔憂自身乳房診療狀況的民眾提供專屬支援專線。隨著調查持續進行，重點仍放在找出所有受害病患，並確保他們獲得所需的資訊與支持，以走出陰霾。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To fail to support or help someone as they expected.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於日常對話，這裡指醫院未能達到應有的照護標準。文中：He stated that the trust is very sorry to the women and their families who were let down by failures in the hospital's breast services.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To contact someone, often to ask for help or support.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面上有「伸手」之意，這裡指病人主動聯繫醫院尋求協助。文中：They are also examining the experiences of 640 former patients who reached out through a special support line.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A person or thing that is being discussed, described, or dealt with.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「學科」或「主詞」，這裡指調查的對象。文中：This situation is now the subject of a wider investigation.

previousArticles.title: Serious Failures in Hospital Care Exposed in New Reports
previousArticles.summaryEn: New reports have highlighted significant failures in patient care within the National Health Service. In one case, twenty women underwent unnecessary breast removal surgeries due to errors. Another investigation continues to examine how hospital management handled warnings about nurse Lucy Letby. These events have led to calls for major changes in how hospitals listen to staff and protect patients. Authorities are now reviewing past medical cases to ensure those affected receive support.

previousArticles.title: Inquiry Reveals Deep Failures in Letby Hospital Case

The report describes a culture of denial where concerns from doctors were ignored or punished. Experts say the findings show a need for better regulation of hospital managers. Families of the victims were kept in the dark for years about the risks. The government has promised to make significant changes to ensure patient safety.

previousArticles.title: New Report Demands Major Changes After Hospital Failures in Letby Case
previousArticles.summaryEn: A new public inquiry has exposed deep failures in how the Countess of Chester Hospital handled concerns about nurse Lucy Letby. The report by Justice Kathryn Thirlwall highlights how management ignored warnings from doctors for years. Families were kept in the dark while babies were being harmed. The government is now facing pressure to create a new regulator to oversee hospital managers. This report serves as a final call for better accountability in the health service.

quiz.question: According to the article, how many patients were identified as having suffered harm out of the 514 cases reviewed by the trust so far?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第三段，醫院針對 514 個案例進行審查，發現其中 315 名患者受到了傷害。選項 A 的 20 是指接受不必要乳房切除手術的人數；選項 B 的 77 是指在 315 名受害者中遭受「重大傷害」的人數；選項 D 的 640 則是聯絡支援專線的前患者總數，而非審查結果。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the hospital's previous management of breast cancer cases based on the text?

options.A: They prioritized speed over the quality of medical tests.
options.B: They were unaware of any patient complaints until the police intervened.
options.C: They failed to respond effectively to early warnings or patient concerns.
options.D: They intentionally harmed patients to reduce hospital costs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第二段提到，院方承認應該要更認真傾聽患者的擔憂，並更早採取行動以防止問題發生，這暗示了院方在危機發生前忽視了警訊。選項 A 並未在文中被提及；選項 B 錯誤，因為院方在警方介入前就已承認缺失；選項 D 為過度推論，文中並無證據顯示這是蓄意行為。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'scrutiny' mean in the context of the NHS?

options.A: A period of financial growth and expansion.
options.B: A process of careful and critical observation or examination.
options.C: A legal requirement to change hospital leadership.
options.D: A state of complete confusion and lack of organization.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。Scrutiny 在此處意指「詳細的審查」或「嚴密的檢視」。文章提到 NHS 正在經歷一段被嚴格檢視的時期，是因為發生了管理失敗與病患安全問題。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 C 與 D 雖然描述了負面狀況，但並非 scrutiny 本身的定義。

quiz.question: What is the primary focus of the article?

options.A: To provide a detailed biography of the victims of medical malpractice.
options.B: To explain the medical procedures involved in breast cancer surgery.
options.C: To report on the failures of a hospital trust and the subsequent investigation into patient safety.
options.D: To criticize the National Crime Agency for its slow response to hospital negligence.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文主要報導 CDDFT 醫院在乳房治療上的重大醫療疏失，以及後續院方的檢討、受害者的經歷以及官方介入調查的狀況。選項 A 僅是文章的一部分細節；選項 B 並非文章重點，文中僅提及手術名稱；選項 D 錯誤，文章並未批評國家犯罪局的辦案速度。
